rule.title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rule.requirement: A landlord may not raise the gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, above the lowest rent charged in the previous 12 months, and no more than twice in 12 months.
rule.key_value: 5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months
rule.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property, including units in mobilehome parks, subject to the listed exemptions; caps increases over any 12-month period and allows at most two increases in 12 months.
rule.exemptions: Affordable deed-restricted housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years (not mobilehomes); separately alienable condos/homes owned by non-corporate owners with notice; owner-occupied two-unit properties; mobilehome owners.
rule.penalty: Owner liable for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess rent charged, and discretionary attorney's fees, plus up to treble damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General or local city attorney may enforce; three-year limitations period.
rule.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rule.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rule.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied residential real property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice; for no-fault just cause the owner must give one month's rent relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rule.key_value: 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
rule.coverage_conditions: Residential real property occupied 12 months or more, except housing certified for occupancy within 15 years, single-family owner-occupied homes with no more than two units or bedrooms, owner-occupied two-unit properties, separately alienable property held by non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elderly and adult residential facilities; school dormitories; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit structures; separately alienable property of non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rule.penalty: Failure to comply renders the termination notice void; an owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct.
rule.interaction: Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and to more protective local ordinances adopted or amended after that date; property is not subject to both.
rule.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

sources.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rule.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest
rule.requirement: Landlords of units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, with a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the year ends.

rule.title: FEHA criminal history and source-of-income screening protections
rule.requirement: Landlords may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not blanket-ban applicants with criminal history. Conviction-based denial must be directly related to tenancy, and source-of-income discrimination, including refusing Section 8 vouchers, is barred.
rule.coverage_conditions: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, apartment managers, and property management companies.
rule.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.
rule.interaction: FEHA invalidates any state law to the extent it purports to require or permit unlawful housing discrimination.
rule.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rule.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
